title: Defending against Adversarial Patches using Dimensionality Reduction
problem: Adversarial patch-based attacks strategically modify localized patches or image areas to deceive trained machine learning models. This significantly reduces model reliability and trustworthiness in deployed systems.
motivation: Adversarial patch attacks are a major deterrent to the reliable and trustworthy deployment of machine learning models in real-world applications.
method: DefensiveDR reduces image complexity by projecting them into a lower-dimensional space using Singular Value Decomposition (SVD, which identifies and keeps only the most important patterns) and t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE, which arranges data in fewer dimensions while preserving similarity). A tunable hyperparameter controls how much information to retain, balancing preservation of classification-critical details against filtering of adversarial perturbations. This preprocessing step substantially mitigates patch-based attacks before images reach any ML model, maintaining accuracy across different architectures.
key_novelty: The defense uses preprocessing that works with any ML model without access to its architecture or outputs, protecting against attackers whether they know the model's internals or not.
contributions: DefensiveDR framework using SVD and t-SNE to defend against adversarial patch attacks
Model-agnostic approach requiring no assumptions about model access or architecture
Improves accuracy from 38.8% to 66.2% against LaVAN and GoogleAp attacks, outperforming LGS (53.86%) and Jujutsu (60%)
Demonstrates robustness against unseen patch-based attacks across various model architectures
primary_theme: Adversarial patch defense via dimensionality reduction
